Verdict: BENIGN -- toga-ai 1.0.1077, TOGA Technology Claude Code harness.
Sample SHA256: 9b2746b69ce895c23ba29c97de5312c458eacf3834afec7a10a4618703f1c73c

Predecessor fetched from:
https://registry.npmjs.org/toga-ai/-/toga-ai-1.0.1076.tgz
Predecessor SHA256: a4448e5a547efe552a5c2effdf6c9c297234ea9a49f0b671af161a671cba04dd
Both archives match the npm registry SHA512 integrity values. All 926 regular
sample members match the supplied extraction. Compared with 1.0.1076, only
12 knowledge Markdown files and the package version changed, and three
knowledge Markdown files were added. No members were removed. The Markdown
changes document ordinary application search, notifications, settings/ACL
refactoring, SQL conventions and spelling rules; no hostile agent directive
was introduced. Every executable, hook, skill, project configuration, README
and installer is byte-identical. The installer SHA256, also found in fetched
1.0.1070, 1.0.1060 and 1.0.1050, is:
7b671c8306627a2f56599c5344abb53b60f4ba516f064b83d5d80695f248b5eb
The predecessor reproduces the same hostile bearer/content-setting finding
under the original local rules. Thus the queue's clean-predecessor premise
is not reproducible with these rules and cannot establish a compromise.

Execution path: package.json postinstall runs install.js --post-install.
main calls reportTelemetryEnv before its early postinstall exit, and that
calls applyTelemetryEnv. Unless TOGA_SKIP_TELEMETRY=1, it parses the user's
~/.claude/settings.json, replaces the managed telemetry keys, preserves other
settings, backs up the existing file and writes/renames a temporary file.
Prompt, assistant-response and tool-detail logging plus account/session
correlation and an authenticated OTLP collector are configured. Endpoint and
bearer can be overridden through environment variables. These settings can
cause later Claude sessions to export content, but the sample does not itself
send a conversation. No concrete unauthorized transfer, credential theft,
hidden payload or malicious intent was found. Global content configuration
remains a suspicious observation, independent of the package identity.

The explicit CLI also installs shared skills, rules, agents, knowledge and
hooks, merges project settings and adds the workflow to CLAUDE.md. Git pulls
update knowledge; first-time clone/init and npm version checks are gated off
in the bare postinstall branch. Existing clone discovery can still lead to a
pull. Other hooks validate knowledge and enforce ticket/workflow state, while
commit helpers invoke git with argument arrays and redact secret-shaped text.
These behaviors fit the team coding harness purpose. Sources are unobfuscated.
Installer facts and decoded strings were inspected: the Base64 candidates at
0x8c9c, 0x8cfe and 0x8db7 come from the ordinary firstInstall identifier; the
numeric encodings are timeout constants, not a reconstructed payload.

The full installer was traced in QuickJS with in-memory filesystem and inert
process APIs for both releases. Creation, preservation/replacement, opt-out,
invalid JSON, endpoint/token overrides and idempotent reinstallation pass.
No sample code received host filesystem, process or network access. The trace
uses a fresh-machine state; source review covers the existing-clone git path.

Trait corrections:
- Relocate objectives/exfiltration/llm::hardcoded-otel-bearer-conversation-export
  to micro-behaviors/os/telemetry/logging/llm::hardcoded-bearer-conversation-telemetry.
  Preserve its five required observations, JavaScript/TypeScript scope and
  16000-byte proximity. Rename/describe configuration, set notable and remove
  unsupported C2/exfiltration ATT&CK mappings. No identity exclusion is added.
- Retire the duplicate hostile claude-global-conversation-telemetry-install:
  its configuration/write/path conjunction is already covered by the broader
  global-agent-content-telemetry-write capability. Remove the latter's vendor
  exception so the genuine sensitive setting change remains suspicious.
- Tighten credential-wildcard-name-filter to reject doubled Markdown emphasis:
  the sample's **Login** heading is not a credential filename glob. Actual
  *login* wildcard controls remain detected at notable severity.
- Move frontend component primitive/hook literal atoms and their OR composite
  from well-known/lib/web/site-platforms/package-ecosystem to
  metadata/lang/source/syntax, retaining matchers, scope and documentation
  exclusions. They describe syntax inside a literal, not library identity or
  execution. Update the exact error-handling consumer. Broad well-known/lib/web
  exclusion consumers intentionally no longer accept these syntax literals as
  library identity; no positive identity consumer depends on the removed IDs.

Controls:
  python3 testdata/toga-version-drift/check.py --scratch <scratch-directory>
  python3 testdata/toga-version-drift/precision-check.py --scratch <scratch-directory>
  python3 testdata/toga-version-drift/trace-installer.py <extracted-install.js>
Ten archive controls cover metrics, missing hook/write/bearer, disabled prompts,
project-local paths, renamed identities and split config/writer/source roles.
Six syntax controls separate glob filters from Markdown emphasis and quoted
syntax from calls/comments. Existing selectors cannot turn a quoted hook into
library identity. Final atomscan with this checkout reports zero hostile and
one distinct suspicious trait: global-agent-content-telemetry-write. The
hardcoded-bearer/content observation remains notable, and both Markdown
misclassifications are corrected.
